story.headline: Panel clears satellite spectrum allocation rules, opening door for Starlink in India
story.body:
The Digital Communications Commission has approved TRAI's recommendations on satellite spectrum allocation, according to the intake note on this story, a step that would clear the way for satellite broadband services in India from Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Reliance Jio.

NDTV Hindi reported on September 9 that Starlink has received a green light from the government, framing the development as opening the way for high-speed internet reach in areas without conventional tower infrastructure. That characterisation is NDTV Hindi's and has not been independently confirmed by this desk.

The wire material available so far does not specify the pricing method for the spectrum, the duration of any allocation, or the conditions attached to it. Those details are not yet confirmed.

No statement from the Department of Telecommunications, TRAI, Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb or Reliance Jio is contained in the material seen so far. No official quotes should be used until obtained directly.

It is also not confirmed from the available material whether this approval is the final regulatory step before commercial launch, or whether separate licensing and security clearances remain outstanding for any of the named operators.

Before publication the desk must confirm: the date and exact wording of the Digital Communications Commission decision; the specific TRAI recommendations accepted, including spectrum pricing and tenure; the current licensing status of Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Reliance Jio; any expected service launch timeline; and on-record comment from the government and the companies. The single wire item here is a Hindi-language report and should be checked against the primary official announcement.
